title: The wrong-hint null for the hinted r=6 and r=7 constructions
supersedes_nothing: This task mints no ledger record and changes no status. It reports measurements only.
scope_statement: Reduced-round AES-128 at r=6 and r=7 on one 4-core machine, one target key, hint-assisted. NOTHING here asserts anything about full-round or deployed AES. No comparison to published cryptanalysis is made in either direction (RQ-AES-003 R3).

findings.label: measured
findings.statement: With the hint bytes taken from the TRUE key schedule, both constructions reproduce BATCH-001 exactly on this binary: 16 of 16 diagonals across 4 true-hint runs (TRUE6, TRUE7 at seed 90001 under contention; TRUE6-S2, TRUE7-S2 at seed 90031 uncontended) have exactly ONE surviving byte and it is the CORRECT byte. r=7 survivors 8034b976 in both runs, identical to BATCH-001 attack7_out.json; r=6 survivors fd,41,fd,7a matching attack6b_out.json rk_last.

findings.label: measured
findings.statement: With ALL THREE hint bytes per diagonal taken from an INDEPENDENT WRONG key, the filter admits NO survivor. Across 44 diagonals from 11 completed trials (11 distinct secrets.token_hex(16) keys, 11 distinct seeds, 6 at r=6 plus 2 at r=7 uncontended in segment 2, 2 at r=6 plus 1 at r=7 in segment 1) the survivor-count histogram is {0: 44}. Zero unique survivors; the true byte appears nowhere in any survivor set; the wrong key's own corresponding byte appears nowhere either.

findings.label: measured, PRIORITY 1 OF THE RESUMED SEGMENT
findings.statement: THE PARTIAL-HINT ARM. With only 1 of the 3 hint bytes per diagonal wrong (4 trials, r=6 and r=7) and with 2 of 3 wrong (3 trials, r=6 and r=7), the filter again admits NO survivor: 28 diagonals, histogram {0: 28}, zero unique survivors, true byte nowhere in any survivor set. A single false hint byte is enough to empty the candidate set.
findings.what_this_settles: The filter is NOT insensitive to individual hint bytes. It requires EVERY hint byte to be correct. The alternative the coordinator named -- that a 1-of-3-wrong hint might still yield a unique correct survivor, which would have made the isolation weaker than 'needs the true hint' -- IS NOT WHAT WAS MEASURED, at 4 trials at 1-of-3 and 3 trials at 2-of-3.

findings.label: interpretation, stated in the strongest honest form the measurement supports
findings.statement: HYPOTHESIS (B) -- that the filter admits exactly one survivor per diagonal for structural reasons and was correct in BATCH-001 only because the hint it was handed was correct -- IS REFUTED BY THIS MEASUREMENT. A false hint does not produce a different unique survivor; it produces NO survivor, and this holds whether 1, 2, or 3 of the 3 hint bytes per diagonal are false. The uniqueness BATCH-001 observed is therefore not an artefact of the survivor test, and the r=6 and r=7 constructions are consistent with hypothesis (A): hint-assisted isolation of the CORRECT byte, contingent on every supplied hint byte being correct.
findings.revision_from_segment_1: The segment-1 version of this finding carried the caveat that all-wrong hints yielding zero survivors was consistent BOTH with 'the filter needs every hint byte' and with 'the filter is insensitive to some hint bytes'. The segment-2 partial-hint arm removes that ambiguity in favour of the first reading. No segment-1 number was changed; the interpretation was extended by new measurement.
limits_of_this_statement: 11 all-wrong trials, 7 partial trials, 4 true-hint trials. All diagonals in every wrong or partial trial read exactly 0; no borderline case was observed, so no distributional claim about near-miss hints beyond 1-of-3 and 2-of-3 is made.
This says nothing about whether the constructions are USEFUL: r=6 remains dominated (see carried_forward) and r=7 remains not a key recovery.
Toy tier. Nothing here bears on full-round or deployed AES, and no comparison to published cryptanalysis is made in either direction.

findings.label: measured, secondary
findings.statement: The separation is not visible in the bulk survivor count. Surviving (k3,k4) pairs summed over all 16 (diagonal,row) cells, per structure: TRUE6 [4066,32], TRUE7 [4066,32], TRUE6-S2 [4115,29], TRUE7-S2 [4115,29]; all-wrong WRONG6-01 [4108,16], WRONG6-02 [4177,21], WRONG7-02 [4003,11], WRONG6-B01 [4039,17], WRONG6-B02 [4083,8], WRONG6-B03 [4181,18], WRONG6-B04 [4035,9], WRONG6-B05 [4156,16], WRONG6-B06 [4019,18], WRONG7-B01 [4010,17], WRONG7-B02 [4084,17]; partial PART6-1of3-A [4080,8], PART6-1of3-B [4117,16], PART7-1of3-A [4116,15], PART7-1of3-B [4039,13], PART6-2of3-A [4200,23], PART6-2of3-B [3954,12], PART7-2of3-A [4084,11]. After one structure all arms sit near 4000-4200; after two, true arms retain 29-32 pairs and false arms 8-23. The decisive difference is the four-row consistency test, which the true byte passes by construction and which no false candidate passed in any measured diagonal. One structure is not decisive; two are.

segment_1.shortfall: 3 of 8 required all-wrong trials completed; partial-hint arm never started.
segment_1.cause: machine contention from concurrently scheduled producer tasks (coordinator-acknowledged scheduling error), not a defect of the object under test.

failed_or_truncated_runs.detail: Launched concurrently at 1 thread each at 17:31:54Z under load average 12. All five hit their 1150 s timeout (exit status 124) at 17:46 having completed only structure 0 of 2, so no per-diagonal verdict exists. NOT negative mathematical evidence; excluded from every distribution. Their first-structure bulk counts (4047, 4085, 3964, 4107, 4291) are recorded but carry no verdict.

Started 17:29:19Z. At 17:31:20Z the executor killed its driver's GNU timeout wrapper while re-planning; timeout forwarded SIGTERM to the child, which died with 0 bytes of output. An executor protocol deviation, recorded and not repaired. Relaunched as WRONG7-02, which completed and is reported.

segment_2.completed: All priority-1 partial-hint runs, 8 further all-wrong runs, and a matched uncontended true-hint pair. No segment-2 run failed, timed out, or was terminated.

carried_forward_unchanged_from_BATCH-001.statement: The r=6 key recovery WORKS AND IS DOMINATED. It requires 12 hint bytes and, by BATCH-001's own measured numbers, costs 69.39 s against roughly 25 s for exhaustive search over the same hinted residual.

carried_forward_unchanged_from_BATCH-001.label: MEASURED BY BATCH-001, NOT RE-MEASURED HERE. This task did not re-run the cost comparison and reports no cost measurement of its own; its own wall times were taken on a contended machine and are not cost measurements.
carried_forward_unchanged_from_BATCH-001.r7_status: The r=7 run is NOT a key recovery and carries no certificate: the true last round key K7 is supplied as input in BATCH-001 and in every arm here.

what_this_task_does_not_do: It does not declare any hypothesis supported, rejected or closed; that is the Reviewer's and Coordinator's judgment.
It asserts nothing about full-round or deployed AES.
It makes no comparison to published cryptanalysis in either direction.
It does not revisit the r=4 / r=5 relabelling; that stands as BATCH-001 recorded it.
